cards.note: Coastal Northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.
The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.

Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

In this region, the most common tree is the Mallee, typically small in height.

It is characterized by its growth pattern, with multiple stems emerging from it's base.
Termite mounds can sometimes be seen in the Northern Territory and rarely northern WA and QLD. They appear as brown, spiky formations rising out of the ground.
To help differentiate from Queensland, trees are thicker and look more like european/american.

In this region, you will almost always find thiner trunks than new south wales, this helps with differentiating the two, the trunks are often dark or white. the more you go towards the center of Australia, the there are less and less trees, which also become smaller. Towards the center of Australia, the soil is also much more red.
With the exception of urban locations, here you will often find bushes, small height trees, shrubs and red soil.
